title: My Wandering Warrior Existence
titleNative: 迷走戦士・永田カビ
synonyms: Diario di una guerriera single - Il mio matrimonio con me stessa
synopsis: The newest diary manga from the Harvey Award-winning creator of My Lesbian Experience with Loneliness. Nagata Kabi’s groundbreaking autobiographical work has captivated audiences around the globe, starting with the viral online comic about identity that would become the graphic novel My Lesbian Experience with Loneliness . Readers from all backgrounds have been moved by the author’s ability to capture complex emotions through her art and text, giving insight into feelings they may have struggled to articulate themselves. Nagata Kabi’s memoirs, including the Eisner-nominated My Solo Exchange Diary and new release My Alcoholic Escape From Reality , have explored themes of physical and mental illness, sex and sexuality, family, and independence. Follow the newest installment of this trailblazing series with My Wandering Warrior Existence , Nagata Kabi’s exploration of longing for love and marriage. (Source: Seven Seas Entertainment) Note: Includes two extra chapters.

synopsis: The Kozuki family was granted the Black Dragon's blessing, allowing them to heal the sick and purify impurity with their voices alone. But Ayame's life shatters after her parents' death, leaving her at the mercy of her cruel aunt and uncle, who tortured her until she lost her voice. As their daughter, Mari, rises to become the new priestess, Ayame is offered as a sacrifice to the Black Dragon. "Why do I have to die like this? Please help me!" In response to her desperate plea, the Black Dragon appears as a striking man and takes her hand, whisking her away to his realm. Chosen to be the bride of the Black Dragon Saku, Ayame finds herself in the enchanting Black Dragon Manor, suspended between the heavens and the human world. But jealousy ignites in Mari, who vows to reclaim Saku and make Ayame suffer once more. (Source: Pocket Comics)

title: Oosaki-san to Komori-san
synopsis: A pure love story between two people with a 50cm height difference and mismatched appearances and personalities. The new part-timer is... a child!?!? Osaki-san is tall and has a poker face, making her seem intimidating at first glance, but she's actually shy and kind. The new employee who comes to Osaki-san's workplace is Komori-san, who is only 147cm tall and very friendly. These two, who are complete opposites in appearance and personality, find themselves drawn to each other...!? Osaki-san is clumsy and a crybaby, yet a go-getter, and Komori-san is oblivious, laid-back, and a gentle, introverted type. What will become of the love between these two, who are complete opposites and have a 50cm height difference...? This is the first installment of a hilarious and heartwarming survival-of-the-fittest (?) romantic comedy about these two quirky girls. (Source: Kadokawa, translated) Note: Originally self-published on the author's Twitter, it was later acquired by Kadokawa who released the first volume on May 11, 2026.

synopsis: "In exchange for my help with your studies, you must stay let me stay at your house until summer vacation." If I get a failing mark again, my chance to live by myself will be over. So I'm forced to go along with the proposal from Tsukasa, the smartest and most beautiful girl in school. But then I saw them. I saw Tsukasa kissing a girl in the park. Tsukasa, who often annoys me with her abnormal invasions of my personal space, has a “girlfriend." Her yuri friend is against this arrangement because she thinks it's “cheating” even if it's between two girls, but Tsukasa is having none of it. After a while, my grades are improving and I'm beginning to enjoy living with Tsukasa. I know that “it's not cheating if you're not in love with them,” but… I'm okay with it. If I don't think about love, we can all get along and be happy, right? (Source: Dengeki Bunko, translated)
